movie.title: The Plague
movie.overview: A socially awkward tween endures the ruthless hierarchy at a water polo camp, his anxiety spiraling into psychological turmoil over the summer.

videos.name: A Conversation with Charlie Polinger, Steven Breckon, Johan Lenox and Lennox Espy

reviews.author: Brent Marchant
reviews.content: Bullying and calculated ostracism have been around seemingly forever, but, in recent years, such antisocial behavior has increasingly been receiving the disparaging attention it truly deserves. Interestingly, the latest voice added to that welcome chorus of criticism comes from a somewhat unlikely source, the excellent and insightful debut feature film from writer-director Charlie Polinger. Set in a summertime water polo camp for tweeners, the picture follows the exploits of a group of impressionable adolescents who learn valuable life lessons on the dangers of the aforementioned toxic behavior and attitudes. At the center of this psychological thriller is idealistic, socially awkward Ben (skillfully portrayed by rising talent and Critics Choice Award nominee Everett Blunck), who struggles to fit in but, because of his profound sense of compassion and consideration, is often out of step with his more rambunctious (and frequently unkind) peers. He’s confused by the scorn they inflict on others, most notably an unconventional nonconformist named Eli (Kenny Rasmussen), who’s frequently marginalized for his unique views and decisively singular outlook on life. Eli’s circumstances are made worse by the development of a severe skin rash that the bullies (led by alpha male Jake (Kayo Martin)) openly and cruelly refer to as “the plague,” a condition that leads to his orchestrated ostracism. Ben is confused by this persistent ridicule and makes an effort to get to know his victimized colleague. But, in getting close to Eli, Ben also develops the same skin rash, causing him to be subjected to the kind of derision and mocking thrust upon Eli. Ben desperately tries to understand this uncalled-for treatment, frequently consulting his coach (Joel Edgerton), but he’s often on his own to try and sort out this relentless disparagement. Life at what is supposed to be an enjoyable experience quickly becomes a living hell. What makes this story work so effectively is the filmmaker’s skillful handling of the material, treating it almost as if it were constructed like a smart horror film – in many ways more chilling than a picture that needs to resort to gratuitous gore and excessive sensationalism to generate viewer gasps and frights (in this case, particularly at times when it appears the plague might actually be real and not just the menacing psychological fabrication of a bunch of teenage boys). This approach is significantly enhanced by the picture’s atmospheric score and inventive cinematography, adding a scary undercurrent to an otherwise coming of age drama. Admittedly, there are times early on when the script could stand to be a little more sharply focused, but then that could also be chalked up to a reflection of the overwhelming confusion Ben experiences as he seeks to assimilate into this new, and sometimes-disturbing, environment. Some might also legitimately view this tale as somewhat clichéd at times, but the picture’s message truly can’t be overemphasized enough, especially for anyone who has ever been in on the receiving end of such reprehensible treatment. As this Cannes Film Festival and Independent Spirit Award nominee illustrates, there’s no place in this world for this kind of behavior – no matter what environment is involved – and the film drives home that point with clarity, purpose and a mission to prevent it from continuing to plague us all.

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: A socially awkward pre-teen attempts to navigate the brutal social dynamics of a summer water polo camp while his worsening anxiety threatens to consume him.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: Struggling to fit in, a socially awkward tween attends an intense summer water polo camp dominated by a ruthless social hierarchy. As the physical demands and relentless bullying escalate, his internal anxiety spirals into deep psychological turmoil. Isolated from his peers, he must find a way to survive the hostile environment before his mental health completely unravels. The film paints an agonizingly tense portrait of youth isolation and the pressures of adolescent conformity.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: The film follows an introverted, socially awkward pre-teen who is sent away to a rigorous summer water polo camp. Hoping to build confidence and athletic skill, he instead finds himself thrown into a cutthroat environment governed by a toxic hierarchy among the campers. Day after day, the grueling physical training is compounded by relentless emotional torment and ostracization from his peers. As the oppressive summer heat mirrors the pressure mounting inside him, his anxiety quickly metastasizes into acute psychological turmoil. Unable to find an ally among the camp counselors or fellow athletes, his perception of reality begins to blur under the weight of his isolation. The relentless peer pressure and toxic masculinity surrounding him push his mental boundaries to a breaking point. Every practice in the pool becomes a battle for emotional and physical survival as he desperately tries to keep his head above water. Ultimately, the story serves as a chilling, claustrophobic exploration of adolescent vulnerability and the devastating impact of unchecked youth cruelty.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: Set over the course of a sweltering summer, this psychological thriller follows a young tween struggling with profound social anxiety who enters a competitive water polo camp. Expecting an opportunity to grow and make friends, he is instead confronted by a harsh, unforgiving social hierarchy enforced by older, aggressive campers. As the boundary between physical exhaustion and mental unraveling begins to dissolve, the pressure cooker atmosphere of the camp pushes his emotional endurance to its absolute limits.

story_structure.climax: During a critical high-stakes moment at the camp, his physical and mental endurance reaches an absolute breaking point, forcing a decisive confrontation with his fears.
story_structure.conflict: He struggles to navigate a ruthless camp hierarchy, triggering intense internal anxiety and a sense of profound social isolation.
story_structure.resolution: In the aftermath of the crisis, he emerges with a renewed understanding of his personal boundaries, resilience, and sense of self-worth outside the rigid social structure.

story_structure.risingAction: As high-pressure training intensifies, the dynamic among his peers grows increasingly toxic, causing his anxiety to spiral into severe psychological distress.
